archetypes.name: Premature scaling
archetypes.definition: Costs and commitments grow faster than a repeatable, self-supporting demand base.
archetypes.caution: Growth alone is not evidence of failure; compare it with cash generation and demand quality.

archetypes.name: Fixed-cost liquidity crunch
archetypes.definition: Large contractual or operating commitments reduce flexibility as liquidity shrinks.
archetypes.caution: The pattern does not establish that any one obligation caused a failure.

archetypes.name: Unit-economics and liquidity squeeze
archetypes.definition: The cost of serving or acquiring demand remains too high while funding becomes constrained.
archetypes.caution: Company-level metrics may hide improving or declining segments.

archetypes.name: Leverage and refinancing pressure
archetypes.definition: Debt obligations and refinancing conditions become a central constraint on the operating business.
archetypes.caution: A restructuring can enable survival; it is not automatically a failure signal.

archetypes.name: Retail demand and execution erosion
archetypes.definition: Demand loss, inventory issues, or store execution weaken revenue while operating costs remain high.
archetypes.caution: Macro demand shifts and company-specific execution can coexist.

archetypes.name: Governance or control breakdown
archetypes.definition: Decision rights, oversight, disclosures, or incentives appear misaligned with durable risk management.
archetypes.caution: Governance events require primary evidence and should not be used as personality judgments.

archetypes.name: Demand or market shock
archetypes.definition: A change in customer behavior, market prices, or financing conditions quickly challenges an existing model.
archetypes.caution: A shock may reveal pre-existing fragility rather than be the sole cause.

archetypes.name: Operational complexity overload
archetypes.definition: Execution complexity, fragmented systems, or a difficult operating footprint prevent planned efficiency gains.
archetypes.caution: Operational difficulty should be tied to dated evidence, not broad labels.
